title: Forgetting a composite of subbundle divisor classes
statement:
Use finite coefficients [def-pur-conventions]. Let $S$ be separated finite type over $k$, and let $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_r=F$ be a filtration by vector subbundles with line quotients $Q_j$ [def-pur-complete-flag-bundle]. Put $E_j=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(F_j^\vee)$, with projection $\pi_j$ and zero section $z_j$ [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. The inclusion $a_j:E_{j-1}\hookrightarrow E_j$ is the Cartier divisor cut out by the image of the tautological vector in $\pi_j^*Q_j$; its associated line bundle is $\pi_j^*Q_j$. Both $E_j$ and $E_{j-1}$ are smooth over $S$. Let
$$d_j:(a_j)_*A_{E_{j-1}}\longrightarrow A_{E_j}(1)[2]$$
be its supported Cartier class [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. Put $\Theta_0=\operatorname{id}_{A_S}$ and define the nested composite
$$\Theta_j=d_j(j-1)[2j-2]\circ(a_j)_*\Theta_{j-1}:(z_j)_*A_S\longrightarrow A_{E_j}(j)[2j],$$
using the constant-coefficient twist identifications. Then, after precomposing with $A_{E_j}\to(z_j)_*A_S$ to forget support,
$$\operatorname{forg}(\Theta_j)=\pi_j^*\bigl(c_{1,A}(Q_1)\cup\cdots\cup c_{1,A}(Q_j)\bigr).$$
This is a statement about the nested vector subbundles of the total space; it asserts no product of line-quotient sections of an arbitrary section on a singular zero locus.

source.place: Step 2 and Step 4: replace the ill-defined flag product by nested Cartier morphisms on vector subbundles and their projection-formula calculation

proof.text: Use the vector-subbundle and invertible-quotient meanings of [def-pur-complete-flag-bundle]. For the given filtration on $S$, adapted frames are obtained by this elementary local construction: near any point trivialize each $Q_i$, lift its generator locally through $F_i\twoheadrightarrow Q_i$, and shrink to an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ where all finitely many lifts exist. A lifted generator splits $F_i\to Q_i$, since its composite with that surjection is $1$; recursively, a frame of $F_{i-1}$ together with this lift is a frame of $F_i$. Thus $F_i|_U=\mathcal O_Ue_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathcal O_Ue_i$ simultaneously for every $i$. This applies to any filtration in the statement, without identifying it with the universal filtration on a flag bundle. The relative-spectrum description [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section], applied to the locally free module $F_j^\vee$, gives $E_j|_U=\operatorname{Spec}R[t_1,\ldots,t_j]$: the dual basis freely generates its symmetric algebra. The inclusion $a_j$ is the quotient setting $t_j=0$, and the image of the tautological vector in $\pi_j^*Q_j$ is $t_j$ times the quotient-frame vector. Multiplication by $t_j$ is injective over every $R$, since it shifts the coefficients of a polynomial. Thus this section cuts out exactly $E_{j-1}$ as an effective Cartier divisor. Apply the last clause of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] to obtain $\mathcal O_{E_j}(E_{j-1})\cong\pi_j^*Q_j$. This argument uses local frames only; a globally split flag is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 01X0, lemma-characterize-OD (2); explicit polynomial calculation for the subbundle section

proof.text: In the charts of Step 1, the projections are $\mathbf A^j_U\to U$ and $\mathbf A^{j-1}_U\to U$, so [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] makes them smooth. Smoothness is affine-local by the equivalent affine-local definition in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; hence $E_j$ and $E_{j-1}$ are smooth over $S$. They are separated finite-type $k$-schemes: their projections are affine, with finitely generated polynomial algebras on the base charts, and $S$ is separated finite type. More explicitly, an adapted finite affine covering exists since $S$ is quasi-compact; its preimages are affine polynomial spectra, and the relative diagonal is locally cut out by $t_i\otimes1-1\otimes t_i$. These are precisely the finite-type and separatedness conditions of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $a_j$ the complementary open is locally $D(t_j)$, and for $z_j$ it is $\bigcup_{i=1}^jD(t_i)$, so both complementary open immersions are quasi-compact. Moreover $a_j$ is proper: after any base change it is still locally the spectrum of a quotient algebra, hence a closed map, and its diagonal is an isomorphism onto a closed subscheme; its local quotient algebra has one relation and is finitely generated. This verifies the properness required in Step 4 directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tags 01V5 and 00T7 (affine-local smoothness and polynomial charts); elementary diagonal and principal-open calculations

proof.text: Write $\rho_j:A_{E_j}\to(z_j)_*A_S$ and $q_j:A_{E_j}\to(a_j)_*A_{E_{j-1}}$ for restriction of constants. By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] and Step 2, every closed direct image here is exact at the finite coefficient ring $A$. Thus it also denotes its derived functor. Direct-image composition is the canonical one: on a test object it evaluates successively on its fibre products, which associate. Since $z_j=a_jz_{j-1}$, this gives $(z_j)_*=(a_j)_*(z_{j-1})_*$ and $\rho_j=(a_j)_*\rho_{j-1}\circ q_j$. The latter equality sends every constant section to the same restricted constant on $S$, so is an equality of sheaf morphisms before passing to the derived category. Put $\alpha_j=\Theta_j\rho_j$; this is exactly the forget-support map appearing in the statement.

source.place: Steps 2 and 4: interpret the nested supported morphisms and forgetting support

proof.text:
For $j\geq1$, abbreviate $a=a_j$, $X=E_j$, $Y=E_{j-1}$, $B=A_X$, $T=A_X(j-1)[2j-2]$, and $V=A_X(1)[2]$. The twist conventions [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] give $a^*T=A_Y(j-1)[2j-2]$. The finite twist is locally constant of rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]; its positive tensor powers are again locally free of rank one by the local tensor calculation $A\otimes_A A=A$. Consequently $T$ has a bounded constructible ordinary etale witness of finite Tor amplitude (one shifted flat sheaf), with its pro-etale realization. Take the witness $\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$, $\ell^NA=0$, and its tensor powers, using the canonical reduction comparison of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Apply [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] to the proper closed immersion $a$, $K=A_Y$, and this $T$. Its proper counit-defined projection isomorphism is
$$P_T:(a_*A_Y)\otimes_A^LT\xrightarrow{\sim}a_*a^*T.$$
The same formula with the coefficient unit is the identity. Under the constant-coefficient twist identifications in the question, the shifted-twisted divisor map is precisely
$$\widetilde d_j=(d_j\otimes1_T)P_T^{-1}:a_*a^*T\to V\otimes T=A_X(j)[2j].$$
The even shift comparison is that of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus].

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; finite etale-origin invertibility supplied by the cited finite projection-formula node

proof.text:
We need the projection map at a morphism, not just an isomorphism of its objects. For $x:B\to T$, naturality and the tensor-unit normalization of the counit-defined projection map [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] give
$$a_*(a^*x)=P_T(1_{a_*A_Y}\otimes x),$$
with $P_B=1$. This normalization is the same proper projection map as in Step 4. Composing with $q_j$ therefore yields the explicit identity
$$P_T^{-1}a_*(a^*x)q_j=(1\otimes x)q_j=q_j\otimes x.$$
Here the last equality uses the unit identifications $B=B\otimes B$ and bifunctoriality of tensor. Equivalently, $P_T(q_j\otimes1_T)$ is the adjunction unit at $T$: its adjunct is $(\varepsilon_{A_Y}a^*q_j)\otimes1_{a^*T}=1_{a^*T}$ by the triangle identity. This checks the restriction map in the formula as well as its tensor-unit normalization.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map: naturality in K and the adjunction triangle identity at the tensor unit

proof.text:
Induct on $j$. Put $C_0=1_A$ and $C_{j-1}=c_{1,A}(Q_1)\cup\cdots\cup c_{1,A}(Q_{j-1})$ as a morphism $A_S\to A_S(j-1)[2j-2]$. For $j=0$, $E_0=S$, $z_0=\mathrm{id}$, and $\Theta_0=\mathrm{id}$, so $\alpha_0=\mathrm{id}=\pi_0^*C_0$. Suppose $\alpha_{j-1}=\pi_{j-1}^*C_{j-1}$. Set $x=\pi_j^*C_{j-1}:A_{E_j}\to T$. Since $\pi_ja_j=\pi_{j-1}$, functoriality of pullback identifies $a_j^*x$ with $\alpha_{j-1}$. The tensor/pullback and shift comparisons used here are canonical by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. Substituting the restriction-map factorization of Step 3 into the definition of $\Theta_j$ gives
$$\alpha_j=\widetilde d_j\, (a_j)_*\alpha_{j-1}\,q_j.$$
This formula is valid on the ambient ordinary derived categories; it requires no smooth-purity isomorphism.

source.place: Step 4, property L4: induction on the number of nested subbundles, with the rank-zero base case written out

proof.text:
Insert the formula of Step 5 into Step 6 and use Step 4:
$$\alpha_j=(d_j\otimes1_T)P_T^{-1}(a_j)_*(a_j^*x)q_j
=(d_j\otimes1_T)(q_j\otimes x)=(d_jq_j)\otimes x.$$
All tensor and target identifications here are the ones defining cup products in [def-pur-supported-cup], with full support for ordinary classes. The shifted tensor identities of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus] therefore identify this map with $(d_jq_j)\cup x$. Step 1 makes $a_j$ an effective Cartier divisor with line bundle $\pi_j^*Q_j$, so [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] gives the actual map equality $d_jq_j=c_{1,A}(\pi_j^*Q_j)$. Consequently
$$\alpha_j=c_{1,A}(\pi_j^*Q_j)\cup\pi_j^*C_{j-1}.$$

source.place: Step 4, property L4: forgetting each Cartier support and the projection-formula multiplication calculation

proof.text:
By the pullback clause of [lem-pur-kummer-additivity], $c_{1,A}(\pi_j^*Q_j)=\pi_j^*c_{1,A}(Q_j)$; the hypotheses hold because Step 2 verified that both schemes are separated finite type over $k$. Cup functoriality and graded commutativity in [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality], applied with full supports, now give
$$\alpha_j=\pi_j^*\bigl(c_{1,A}(Q_j)\cup C_{j-1}\bigr)
=\pi_j^*\bigl(C_{j-1}\cup c_{1,A}(Q_j)\bigr).$$
The sign is $(-1)^{2(2j-2)}=1$. Associativity identifies the right-hand side with the required ordered product of $j$ first Chern classes. This completes the induction, including $j=1$, and proves the asserted equality for every $0\leq j\leq r$.
